samples.summary: `snapshotJsonRoot`'s control-character fallback cannot work — both branches go through the same broken `toJSON()` string, and unlike the script it cites there is no control-char repair or proxy-walk fallback, so copying an affected sheet/slides/board document throws (500) instead of succeeding
samples.evidence: `snapshotJsonRoot` does `JSON.parse(doc.toJSON())`, and on failure `asJsonRoot(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(doc.getRoot())))`. The Yorkie root proxy's own `toJSON()` returns the *same* JSON string (that is exactly what the docstring says makes `JSON.stringify(root)` double-encode), so `JSON.stringify(root)` produces a quoted copy of that string; `asJsonRoot` then unwraps the string layer with a plain `JSON.parse(value)` and hits the identical unescaped control character, throwing `SyntaxError` again. The reference implementation `packages/backend/scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts` needs two extra things this omits: `parseJsonSnapshot` (lines 81-94), which re-parses after escaping control chars, and a third fallback `detachYorkieValue(sourceDoc.getRoot())` (line 326) that walks the proxy manually. The new unit test at document-copy.service.spec.ts ("falls back to the root proxy when toJSON is unparseable") passes only because its fake `getRoot()` returns a *plain* object with no `toJSON`, so it does not exercise the real path.

samples.summary: `CopySource` is fully percent-encoded, including the bucket/key separator (`/` → `%2F`); if the storage backend does not unescape the header the copy fails at runtime for every blob-backed document
samples.evidence: `CopySource: encodeURIComponent(`${this.bucket}/${this.storageKey(id)}`)` encodes the separating slash (and any prefix slash) as `%2F`. The AWS SDK passes this straight into `x-amz-copy-source`. The unit test only asserts against the mocked command args, and the task notes (docs/tasks/active/20260813-document-copy-lessons.md:32-36) explicitly say the MinIO `CopyObject` path was never exercised locally. If the backend does not URL-decode the header, every pdf/image/file copy 500s with NoSuchKey/InvalidArgument.
searchedFor: grep CopySource/CopyObject across repo — this is the only usage

samples.summary: Rollback deletes the copied blob even when the row deletion failed, leaving a surviving Document row pointing at a blob that no longer exists
samples.evidence: In the `copyContent` failure branch, `deleteDocument` failures are swallowed by `.catch(...)` (only logged), and control falls through unconditionally to `await this.discardBlob(fileId)`. If the row delete failed, the copy row survives with `fileId` referencing a now-deleted S3 object, so every subsequent download of that document 404s. The blob discard should be conditional on the row actually being removed.

samples.summary: Row-menu "Make a copy" is not disabled while a copy is in flight, so repeated clicks fire multiple copies
samples.evidence: The bulk-bar button guards with `disabled={copyDocumentsMutation.isPending}` (line ~1210), but the `DropdownMenuItem` version calls `copyDocumentsMutation.mutate({ ids: [String(doc.id)] })` with no pending guard. Since each copy is a separate non-idempotent POST, a double-click produces two documents (`… (copy)` and `… (copy 2)`).

samples.summary: `copyContent` silently no-ops for any document type outside the known set, so a future/unknown type produces an empty copy reported as success
samples.evidence: `if (!JSON_ROOT_TYPES.has(type)) return;` sits after the `doc`/`note` arms and after the blob types are (correctly) treated as no-ops. Any type not in {doc, note, sheet, slides, board, pdf, image, file} — i.e. any type added later without touching this file — silently yields a content-less copy rather than failing loudly, which is the exact 'empty document claiming to be a copy' outcome the rollback comment says must never happen. `yorkieDocKeyPrefix` throws for unknown types precisely so such mistakes surface, but it is never reached on this path.

The Yorkie root proxy's own `toJSON()` returns the *same* JSON string (that is exactly what the docstring says makes `JSON.stringify(root)` double-encode), so `JSON.stringify(root)` produces a quoted copy of that string; `asJsonRoot` then unwraps the string layer with a plain `JSON.parse(value)` and hits the identical unescaped control character, throwing `SyntaxError` again. The reference implementation `packages/backend/scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts` needs two extra things this omits: `parseJsonSnapshot` (lines 81-94), which re-parses after escaping control chars, and a third fallback `detachYorkieValue(sourceDoc.getRoot())` (line 326) that walks the proxy manually. verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as described. snapshotJsonRoot (document-copy.service.ts:290-300) falls back to asJsonRoot(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(doc.getRoot()))), and asJsonRoot (303-312) unwraps nested string layers with a plain JSON.parse. Per the file's own docstring (279-281), the Yorkie root proxy's toJSON returns the same JSON string as doc.toJSON() (that is why JSON.stringify(root) double-encodes), so the fallback re-parses the identical unescaped control character and throws the same SyntaxError — the documented control-char rescue cannot work. The cited reference script does contain the two missing pieces: parseJsonSnapshot with escapeControlCharsInJson (copy-yorkie-documents.ts:81-94, used in normalizeSnapshot's unwrap loop at 99-101) and the third fallback detachYorkieValue(sourceDoc.getRoot()) at line 326. The path is reachable on a real flow: copyContent routes sheet/slides/board (186-193) through snapshotJsonRoot, and the throw propagates out of copy() after rollback (102-118), i.e. a 500. The unit test at document-copy.service.spec.ts:312-322 does not exercise this because its fake getRoot() returns a plain object with no toJSON, so JSON.stringify walks it structurally. No guard elsewhere prevents this, and it is squarely in the correctness lane (error handling that mis-handles failures / ineffective fallback causing a crash).

finding.summary: `CopySource` is fully percent-encoded, including the bucket/key separator (`/` → `%2F`); if the storage backend does not unescape the header the copy fails at runtime for every blob-backed document
finding.evidence: `CopySource: encodeURIComponent(`${this.bucket}/${this.storageKey(id)}`)` encodes the separating slash (and any prefix slash) as `%2F`. The AWS SDK passes this straight into `x-amz-copy-source`. The unit test only asserts against the mocked command args, and the task notes (docs/tasks/active/20260813-document-copy-lessons.md:32-36) explicitly say the MinIO `CopyObject` path was never exercised locally. If the backend does not URL-decode the header, every pdf/image/file copy 500s with NoSuchKey/InvalidArgument.
searchedFor: grep CopySource/CopyObject across repo — this is the only usage

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as the reviewer quoted: file.service.ts:145 sets `CopySource: encodeURIComponent(`${this.bucket}/${this.storageKey(id)}`)`, which percent-encodes the bucket/key separator (and any prefix separator built at file.service.ts:63-65) as %2F. It is reachable on a real, ungated path: document.controller.ts:307 -> document-copy.service.ts:74 (`await this.fileService.copy(source.fileId)`) for every pdf/image/file document copy; nothing rewrites or validates CopySource in between. The unit tests cannot detect the problem: file.service.spec.ts:22 mocks CopyObjectCommand and the assertions at :166 and :181-183 re-apply encodeURIComponent to construct the expected value, so they pass for whatever encoding the implementation emits. docs/tasks/active/20260813-document-copy-lessons.md:32-36 confirms the MinIO CopyObject path was never exercised locally. No refutation ground applies: the code is as described (not `not-present`), no guard makes it unreachable (not `already-guarded`), and a failing server-side copy on the main copy flow is core runtime correctness (not `out-of-scope`). A `counterexample` refutation would require proving the storage backend URL-decodes the whole header before splitting bucket from key; that is server-side behavior I cannot establish from this repo, and node_modules/@aws-sdk is not installed so I could not even check whether the SDK serializer passes the header verbatim or double-encodes it. Reference AWS SDKs encode copy sources in path mode, which preserves '/', so this is at minimum a deviation from the conventional contract. Uncertainty about whether it fires is not grounds to drop it.

finding.summary: Whole-root JSON snapshot copies comment threads for sheet/slides/board, contradicting the "comments are never carried over" invariant
finding.evidence: `copyContent`'s JSON arm assigns *every* root key from the source snapshot onto the copy (lines 187-198). Sheet comments live inside the Yorkie root — `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:4` (`ws.comments`) and `packages/frontend/src/app/documents/document-detail.tsx:244` reads `docRoot.sheets[...].comments`. So a copied spreadsheet carries all of the source's comment threads (with their authors' user ids, names and photos), while the `doc`/`pdf` arms deliberately drop them (`readDocsRoot` only reads content/pageSetup/stylesJson). The class docstring (line 33-37) and docs/design/document-copy.md:33 both state comments are deliberately not carried over — the sheet/slides/board path violates that.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. The JSON-root arm of `copyContent` does not write the raw snapshot: `document-copy.service.ts:198` applies `const content = stripComments(snapshot)` and the write loop at 203-205 iterates `content`, not `snapshot`. `stripComments` (225-238) empties the root-level `comments` map and, for every entry of `sheets`, replaces `worksheet.comments` with `{}` — precisely the `sheets[tabId].comments` path the finding says is carried over (confirmed as the real storage location by yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:3-5 and worksheet-document.ts:94,140-147). The maps are emptied rather than deleted deliberately, matching `createWorksheet`'s seeding of `comments: {}` (worksheet-document.ts:140-147). The docstring at 213-224 and docs/design/document-copy.md:36-42 document this stripping, so the stated invariant is upheld rather than violated. Grep for `comments` under slides/board found only an unrelated prose mention (slides-image-input.ts:161), so no analogous unstripped path exists for the other JSON-root types.

finding.summary: Snapshot round-trip demotes Yorkie Long values to 32-bit Integers, corrupting timestamps in copied roots
finding.evidence: The JSON arm writes `root[key] = value` with values that came out of `JSON.parse`, i.e. plain JS numbers. The repo documents that Yorkie 0.7.x stores any integer-valued JS number as a 32-bit Integer, which is why comment timestamps are written as bigint (`BigInt(ms) as unknown as number`) in packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:8-14. Copying a sheet root therefore writes `createdAt` (~1.78e12) back as a plain number, truncating it to its low 32 bits — the copy's comment/any Long field decodes as a 1970 date. `scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts:115-118` (the cited precedent) has an explicit bigint branch; this implementation has none.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts the JSON arm writes `root[key] = value` with plain JSON.parse numbers and "has none" of the bigint conversion, truncating Long timestamps. The code does not match that description. document-copy.service.ts:204 writes `(root as JsonRoot)[key] = reviveLongs(value);`, and `reviveLongs` at lines 254-271 converts every integer-valued number outside [INT32_MIN, INT32_MAX] (lines 240-241, 257-260) to `BigInt(value) as unknown as number`, recursing through arrays (262) and nested objects (263-269) so nested `createdAt` (~1.78e12) is coerced to bigint before assignment. The doc comment at 243-253 explicitly cites the Yorkie 0.7.x 32-bit Integer behavior and the frontend `toYorkieMs` precedent, which I confirmed at yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:8-14. A Grep for reviveLongs/snapshotJsonRoot/stripComments shows the snapshot flows only through the single guarded write at lines 189-209, so there is no bypassing call site reaching the Yorkie write without the coercion.

finding.summary: snapshotJsonRoot has no control-character fallback, so `JSON.parse(doc.toJSON())` throws and the whole copy fails for affected documents
finding.evidence: `snapshotJsonRoot` does a bare `JSON.parse(doc.toJSON())`. The docstring claims "same handling as scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts", but that script explicitly wraps the same call in a try/catch because "Some documents contain control characters that Yorkie's raw JSON string path does not escape correctly" (packages/backend/scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts:316-327, with `escapeControlCharsInJson` and a `detachYorkieValue` fallback). Without those fallbacks a sheet/slides/board root containing a control character makes the copy throw a SyntaxError, rolling the copy back and surfacing a 500 to the user.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `snapshotJsonRoot` performs a bare `JSON.parse(doc.toJSON())` with no control-character fallback. The code does not match that description: document-copy.service.ts:294-299 wraps the parse in try/catch and falls back to `asJsonRoot(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(doc.getRoot())))`, rethrowing only when no `getRoot` is available. The docstring at :284-288 names the control-character case as the exact reason for the fallback, mirroring copy-yorkie-documents.ts:313-328 (the script's second tier is identical; only the extra best-effort `detachYorkieValue` third tier is absent, which is not the claimed defect and does not cause a throw on control characters). Tests at document-copy.service.spec.ts:312-322 feed a toJSON string containing a literal U+0001 and assert the copy still succeeds via the getRoot fallback, with :324-333 asserting rethrow only when both paths fail. The described crash/rollback path therefore does not exist as stated.
